full_judgment: 5. The High Court Division, after hearing, except in Writ Petition No. 1499 of 2004, made all other Rules absolute holding that under SRO No. 206 dated 17.9.98 customs duty, VAT, IDSO and AIT on the import of power tillers and its accessories during the period from 15.9.1998 to 30.6.1999, were exempted and the above exemption was given in public interest i.e for the interest of agriculture, so not without any reason, and further the above exemption was meant for imports made within particular period; the contention of the learned Assistant Attorney General that the respondents were not entitled to refund as their claim for refund was now barred by limitation as they did not pray for refund within the statutory period of six months from the date of the assessment has no basis when admittedly no final assessment of the duty payable on the imported goods was made by the petitioner till date and further the provisional assessment was made by them after 3/4 months of the arrival of the goods without recording any reason whatsoever and the failure to make any final assessment on the imported goods till date has not been explained by the petitioners who had the statutory duty to do so under the Customs Act; the very purpose of said SRO 206 date 17.9.2008 for public good has been frustrated by the action of the petitioners and so apart from taking proper action against the delinquents officers with information to the High Court Division, the petitioners are also bound to refund the duty, tax and other charges collected in excess in violation of said SRO No.206 dated 17.9.98. The High Court Division however discharged the Rule issued in Writ Petition No. 1499 of 2004 on the ground that in the above case the bill of entry being submitted on 1.9.1999, i.e beyond the notified period under said SRO No. 206 dated 17.9.98, the petitioner of the above writ petition was not entitled to exemption as provided by the said SRO.
